device.modelDescription: Scenario module of the ch-packs family: one tool, ci_failure_triage, that answers "why did CI fail?" from GitHub Actions through ch-access-github and the step modules, with the failing step, the error lines, the cross-run history and a measured receipt.

actionList.name: ci_failure_triage
actionList.description: Call this first when a CI run failed. It answers why: the failing run, job and step, every failed job of the run with its failing step and first error (it cannot tell which jobs gate the run: a continue-on-error job fails the same way), the few error lines (redacted), whether the failure is new, flaky or recurring across the last runs with the commit where it first appeared, the GitHub logins who last touched it, and coverage that says what it could not read (expired, truncated or unavailable logs, the log cap) and whether the history was just rebuilt after a change of failure signature, when its counts can be low. The repository is the one you are working in; pass repo: 'owner/name' to choose another, and run_id for a run other than the latest failed one. When no run failed it says so and names the latest success. The summary ends with a receipt sentence (what was read, in how many calls); show it verbatim.
